A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSD research. Their text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison despite changes in placement.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning-benchmark, computational-efficiency and ablation results, including additional experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and adds reward-model robustness and AlpacaEval results in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the mixture and acceptance mechanisms remain unchanged. Section 4 adds a limited scoring-component adaptation: an outcome reward model replaces the process reward model and scores intermediate steps during general-domain generation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mathematical and scientific reasoning, including the appendix datasets. v3 retains this coverage and adds open-ended general-domain generation on AlpacaEval. This substantially broadens task requirements; using general-purpose models on reasoning benchmarks in v1 did not provide equivalent coverage.

E2.justification: The existing SD, voting, Best-of-N and beam-search comparisons are retained. The added AlpacaEval evaluation introduces GPT-4 Turbo reference outputs as a comparison opponent. Table 5's additional Qwen PRMs are RSD configurations, not new competing decoding methods.

E3.justification: Existing reasoning protocols remain unchanged. Added experiments evaluate Qwen PRMs of 7B and 72B parameters and introduce an AlpacaEval2.0 win-rate protocol using 805 prompts, Llama draft/target models and an ORM threshold of zero. These are supplementary settings, not revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds a focused test of dependence on reward-model family and size using Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B and 72B. The original threshold, weighting-function, reasoning-complexity and model-merging analyses remain unchanged, including those in Appendix B.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run information, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and appendix scores are retained. Table 5 adds average accuracies of 65.9 and 66.5 for Qwen PRMs of 7B and 72B. Table 6 adds AlpacaEval win rates of 7.09% for draft-only, 24.47% for target-only and 18.85% for RSD; the text also reports 65% draft-generated tokens.

T1.justification: The assumptions, mixture definition, Propositions 2.1–2.3 and their Appendix A proofs are retained. Changes in equation and proof placement do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph and conclusion retain the same central claims about reward-guided decoding, threshold optimality and efficiency, including up to 4.4-fold fewer FLOPs and a 3.5-point average accuracy advantage. The additional experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds interpretations concerning robustness to PRM choice and applicability with an ORM, while noting the lack of a suitable general-domain PRM and limited threshold tuning. Section 3.1 also recasts unchanged general-model results as showing larger improvements, rather than merely aligning with math-specific models.

D1.justification: v1 offers code privately upon request pending public release; v3 states availability at a public GitHub repository. The new experiments document checkpoint identifiers, prompt count, ORM score range and threshold. Existing hardware, backend and model-merging details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations supporting AlpacaEval, Skywork-Reward, Qwen PRMs and Q# post-training, and removes the ApiQ citation. The central positioning relative to speculative decoding and reasoning reward models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited introductory edits, expanded beam-size terminology, two added Discussion passages, a shortened specialized-PRM paragraph and new acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 5–6 are added; Table 5 partly redisplays existing Table 2 results. Figure 1 is resized, Algorithm 2 and Table 1 exchange positions, and several figures and appendix tables move. Existing plots retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence beyond one PRM family, adds an informative general-domain evaluation and improves code-access documentation. These are useful but bounded gains: AlpacaEval RSD remains below target-only performance, and the reported draft-token share does not establish an end-to-end speed advantage. The original scientific core and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
